who_for: A 4K monitor makes sense if you spend hours looking at text, spreadsheets, code, or photos. At 27 inches, 4K resolution makes text noticeably sharper than a 1440p screen and gives you room to put two windows side by side.

If you mainly play fast competitive games, a high-refresh 1440p monitor is often the better value. If you're plugging in a laptop, look for USB-C with power delivery, which lets one cable handle video, charging, and accessories.

how_we_picked.label: Panel type
how_we_picked.text: IPS and IPS Black panels hold color and contrast at an angle better than VA and TN panels, which matters for desk work and photo editing.

how_we_picked.label: Color accuracy
how_we_picked.text: For creative work we favored monitors that ship factory-calibrated, with a published report or a Calman or Pantone verification.

how_we_picked.label: Refresh rate
how_we_picked.text: 60Hz is fine for office work. For gaming we looked for 144Hz or faster, plus a quick response time.

how_we_picked.label: Connectivity
how_we_picked.text: USB-C with enough wattage to charge a laptop, a built-in hub, and a KVM switch can replace a separate dock.

how_we_picked.label: Value
how_we_picked.text: We compared each monitor's price with the features it actually adds, because many 4K panels are close in image quality.
